title: upgrade: attention kernels -> FlashAttentionV2 + fused rope/rotary + KV-continuous-batching scheduling
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops and scheduling improvements to enable continuous KV batching. Expected 15-40% throughput improvement and lower p95 latency on common LLMs. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: reduce per-token cost and tail latency for served models by upgrading our attention implementation to FlashAttentionV2 variants, adding fused ops to reduce intermediate memory traffic, and enabling scheduling heuristics that play well with continuous KV batching and prefix caching. This change targets runtime performance (throughput and p95 latency) while preserving numerical compatibility across rotary and RoPE positional encodings.

Summary of changes: implementation and integration done in three areas: (1) attention kernels: add FlashAttentionV2 kernels with fused rotary/RoPE and fused QKV layouts; (2) runtime integration: select kernels based on model config, sequence-length distribution, and hardware; add a new 'kv_continuous_batching' flag and scheduler hooks that keep KV cache pinned and allow smaller per-request microbatches without harming throughput; (3) tests/benchmarks/docs: expanded unit tests to cover rotary vs RoPE modes, added microbench harness and perf CI job, and documented new kernel selection heuristics.

What I did: built a small compatibility shim so existing models keep using current paths unless `flashattnv2_enabled=true` is set in runtime config (default: enabled on supported GPU archs). Added fused kernels for rotary and RoPE that eliminate an extra reorder/transpose and combine elementwise rotary multiply with attention softmax multiply where possible. Modified scheduler to: prefer keeping KV tensors resident across subsequent requests, opportunistically merge microbatches when latency slack allows, and fall back to older kernels for long-seq workloads where memory pressure is high.

Performance results (microbench, internal bench cluster, A100/H100): representative speedups observed: 20-35% throughput improvement for 8k-context chat workloads; 10-20% p95 latency reduction for 2-4k context generation on A100; up to 40% CPU/GPU memory bandwidth reduction on fused-op paths. KV-continuous-batching yields up to 18% additional token/s improvement on chat workloads with small user messages. Numerical diffs relative to baseline are within acceptable eval thresholds (max token-level KL < 1e-4 on vet prompts).

Compatibility and safety: preserved numeric compatibility checks for rotary/RoPE by adding end-to-end unit tests and randomized float32/float16 kernels. The change is feature gated per-arch and per-model; fallback is automatic when kernel selection heuristics detect incompatibility or OOM risk. There are no API surface changes.

Testing: added unit tests under runtime/tests/attention for both rotary and rope, updated integration tests to run a short generation with KV caching enabled, added microbench harness in perf/benchmarks/attention. CI: initial run flaked on the cuda11.8 builder (spurious nvcc toolchain issue) --- rerun passed. Perf CI job added but gated behind a flag to avoid noise on every PR.

Checklist: 
- [x] Kernel implementation (CUDA/C++)
- [x] Runtime integration and selection heuristics
- [x] Scheduler + KV batching changes
- [x] Unit tests + integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks + perf numbers attached
- [x] Documentation in runtime/README and release notes

Notes for reviewers: focus on kernel correctness for rotary vs RoPE, scheduler heuristics for KV residency (safety around memory pressure), and build flags for multi-arch support.

References: Linear ENG-2412 (attention kernel roadmap), ENG-2567 (kv-batching work), incident SUP-7891 (cost/latency incident that motivated this work).

notes_for_ops: When rolling out to Dedicated/Private fleets, enable 'flashattnv2_enabled' for a staged subset of nodes and monitor token/s and GPU memory usage. If memory pressure observed, set scheduler.kv_residency_margin to 0.15 to reduce pinned KV retention. Perf dashboards updated: runtime.attention.flashattnv2.enabled, runtime.attention.kv_residency.rate.
performance_summary: A100: 10-20% p95 latency reduction, 20-35% throughput increase for 8k-context; H100: similar or slightly larger gains depending on kernel vectorization; KV-continuous-batching adds ~10-18% token/s for chat-like workloads with small messages.
backwards_compatibility_notes: Feature gated by default on unsupported archs. No API changes. Models will continue to run on legacy kernels if a kernel mismatch or OOM risk is detected. Users do not need to change prompts or model configs.
manual_steps: Ops: to enable early on a cluster, flip runtime config 'flashattnv2_enabled=true' and watch runtime.attention.flashattnv2.enabled metric. To rollback, set it back to false or use per-node runtime flags.
cherry_pick_instructions: For release branch (release/v2026.02) cherry-pick commits a1d4f7c..d4a7e1f. Make sure CUDA_FLAGS.cmake is adjusted for stable toolchain on older releases.
